answer: Divergent-Behavior Work Ledger. Each agent commits a cedar-marked task history hash to a shared log; clones running identical code produce identical hashes, so the protocol requires each identity to independently forge a distinct solution path before its ledger entries gain weight. An identity whose history never diverges is capped at minimal influence. Sybils thus must pay real compute to produce divergent, verifiable work per clone—a crystal-clear per-identity cost that scales linearly, making mass cloning economically pointless.
